notes: Tier 1 (read-only) + Tier 2 (install/enable/disable/restart/uninstall, plus custom-image install, tag edit, container log, and add/delete manifest) of the 'Example 1' extension, williangalvani.example1 (docker williangalvani/blueos-example1). Vehicle restored to pre-capture state (only default blueos.major_tom remains; only default manifest). CPU/RSS via tools/sample_resource.sh; latencies via tools/probe_http.sh. Raw evidence: kraken_sample_running.json, kraken_sample_with_ext.json, kraken_slo_running.json.

route_inventory.note: v2.0 exposes ~40 routes (extension/container/manifest/jobs); v1.0 is the legacy flat surface. Full list from /kraken/v{ver}/openapi.json.

running_baseline.note: GET-endpoint contracts on a healthy running kraken with only the default major_tom extension installed.

GET /stats.body_predicate: object keyed by container -> {cpu, disk, memory}

GET /manifest/consolidated.body_predicate: large consolidated manifest of all extensions across sources

GET /stats.note: ~2s: aggregates live Docker stats for all containers

with_extension_installed.note: kraken's own footprint is unchanged by installing/running an extension: extensions run out-of-process as separate Docker containers, so kraken RSS/CPU is independent of installed-extension count

transitions.note: Tier 2 lifecycle of williangalvani.example1 (docker williangalvani/blueos-example1:v1.0.1). Timings are single-shot observations, not distributions.

install.effect: streams docker pull progress as base64-encoded JSON fragments; ends 'Downloaded newer image for williangalvani/blueos-example1:v1.0.1'; creates and starts container extension-williangalvaniblueosexample1v101; adds entry to installed_extensions and settings extensions[]

disable.effect: stops and removes the extension container (GET /container/ no longer lists it); settings entry enabled -> false

enable.effect: returns immediately (async); container comes up within ~3s; settings entry enabled -> true

restart.effect: accepted (async, body null); container recreated (Up ~2s afterward)

uninstall.effect: accepted (async, body null); removes container and image reference; installed_extensions and settings extensions[] revert to default (only blueos.major_tom)

custom_install.effect: custom-image install (blue plus flow): accepts a full ExtensionSource {identifier,tag,name,docker,enabled,permissions}, streams docker pull progress, creates+starts the container. Captured installing williangalvani.example1:v1.0.0 (docker williangalvani/blueos-example1)

tag_edit.effect: switches an installed extension to a different tag (dev/alternative version); pulls the new tag image and recreates the container. Captured switching williangalvani.example1 v1.0.0 -> v1.0.1 (settings tag updated)

container_log.effect: returns the extension container log as streamed base64-encoded JSON fragments (decoded sample: 'heartbeat')

add_manifest.effect: adds an external manifest source {name,url,enabled}; returns the created manifest with a generated identifier (UUID) and next priority. Captured adding a test manifest then removing it

delete_manifest.effect: removes an external manifest source by identifier

settings_mutations.enable_disable: toggles the extension's enabled boolean in place
settings_mutations.add_manifest: appends to manifests[] (POST /manifest/ -> 201); DELETE /manifest/{id} -> 204 removes it

platform_matrix.note: kraken behavior is platform-independent (Docker/extension management does not depend on the flight-controller board); not captured across boards. Runtime captured on Navigator only.

state_machine: none — kraken has no service-level lifecycle state machine; per-extension enabled/running state lives in settings + Docker, not modeled as kraken states (see service_definition states: Unknown)
